name: pleiotrophin

function.text: PTN is the approved symbol for pleiotrophin. Reviewed functional annotations implicate its product in carbohydrate binding; chondroitin sulfate binding; cell surface receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase signaling pathway.

germline.text: No conflict-free strong or definitive constitutional disease relationship met the source-selection criteria for this draft; this does not exclude a germline association.

somatic.text: Cancer Hotspots v1 reports recurrent residue-level observations in Colorectal carcinoma; Esophageal carcinoma; Lung squamous cell carcinoma. This is statistical recurrence evidence; it does not establish that every variant in this gene is a driver or a clinically actionable alteration. Evidence in this collection is restricted to the historical V1 release.

function.text: PTN encodes pleiotrophin. Based in part on similarity, it binds cell-surface proteoglycan receptor via their chondroitin sulfate (CS) groups. Thereby regulates many processes like cell proliferation, cell survival, cell growth, cell differentiation and cell migration in several tissues namely neuron and bone. It also plays a role in synaptic plasticity and learning-related behavior by inhibiting long-term synaptic potentiation.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving PTN have been reported in colorectal carcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, and gastric adenocarcinoma.
